content:
An experiment to change all haveI in proofs to have (see here #mathlib4 > letI/haveI linter @ 💬 ) caused an unexpected slowdown in mathlib, which led to the discovery that the kernel was taking a surprisingly long time to consume a random proof in commutative algebra (the proof of docs#IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_expChar_pow_of_isSeparable ). Intrigued, I asked Claude to audit all of mathlib and flag the top 50 declarations in mathlib which were slowest to typecheck in the kernel. Sure eough, adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_expChar_pow_of_isSeparable was in the top 20 but there are many more, some 5x as bad. A slightly sloppy LLM-generated summary of the results is here https://gist.github.com/kbuzzard/c5821b44b8bb7de13a5b9342eb96fe1f .

A more careful analysis of adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_expChar_pow_of_isSeparable showed that the proof was abusing defeq, Lean was letting the proof get away with it, and then the kernel was groaning trying to check that it was OK. I have fixed that particular proof in #41664 and the result of getting typechecking down from 11,990,363 mHeartbeats to a sensible value (sensible values are more like 10K mHeartbeats: in fact the median is 3526) actually speeds the entire file up by 20%! (there is also a report that mathlib itself speeds up by a lot but this must be bogus).

If people want to take a look at these files and see if they (or AI) can write proofs which the kernel doesn't find so distasteful then there is probably some low-hanging fruit in that list.

For those who aren't familiar with the part of the system which I'm highlighting here -- these are proofs which might well compile quickly, but then (in VS Code) a one-line-long orange bar
on the theorem name takes a suspiciously long time to go away. What's happening here is that the elaborator has accepted the proof, but the kernel is having a harder time checking that it really works. If you have a copy of mathlib open then search it for theorem powQuotSuccInclusion_injective, watch the file compile, and observe the one orange line staying for several seconds before the two blue ticks appear. The question is: what is going on in that proof that makes the kernel take so long to be convinced that the proof is OK?
I just picked a random theorem from the list and tried making it faster, #41700

theorem powQuotSuccInclusion_injective (i : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (powQuotSuccInclusion p P i) := by
  rintro ⟨x, hx⟩ ⟨y, hy⟩ h
  simpa [Subtype.ext_iff] using h

sorts out the example I flagged above. Edit: #41701

OK so this is having unexpected benefits -- either that or radar is lying to us.

My original golf of number 20 on the list has a radar output which looks like this and my instinct was "OK so -6.6G was about what I was expecting for the file speed-up, and radar also reports -187G for overall instructions but clearly radar is lying to me". And now Aaron's golf of number 9 has radar here reporting that build instructions are down 33G, and then my golf of number 2 has radar reporting -279G here. @Joscha Mennicken are these results genuine? These are PRs which each golf one proof and I would expect the build time of the relevant file to go down, and then I would expect the build time of mathlib in total to go down by pretty much exactly the same amount.

That might just be noise, and you were lucky it was green all three times? E.g. https://radar.lean-lang.org/repos/mathlib4/commits/7c59a0a6cbff267024f1c701907f704c690782fb looks pretty similar, even though it only adds a lemma. Also, your radar links don't show an increase in task-clock (i.e. total CPU time spent compiling, summed across all cores) alongside the instructions.

Yeah this was also my instinct. But my experience with radar is that -279G is quite a surprisingly large amount of noise.

I've set an LLM off to golf the 17 other proofs in the top 20 and if I make one PR with all of them then it seems like it might be a good test for radar.
picked the slowest theorem from the list and tried making it faster, #41703
Yeah, it's quite a bit of noise. Looking at the last few commits on the right, maybe noise is (hopefully just temporarily) worse right now?
picked another random theorem and tried making it faster, #41704
#41705 attempts the top 20, apart from those which were done when I started the LLM
I set it off before #41703 and #41704 so now you can compare and contrast your fix with Opus's.
